data.title: Grammar & Logic Refinement
data.description: Calibration of sentence logic to eliminate common non-native word order traps.

sections.explain: In Standard English, 'have' meaning possession is never used in the -ing form.

words.word: I have a large family in Mumbai.
I am having a large family in Mumbai.
I'm having had a large family in Mumbai.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct way to agree.
sections.explain: 'Agree' is a verb. 'I am agree' is a literal translation of Spanish/Hindi logic.

words.word: I agree with the project timeline.
I am agree with the project timeline.
I am according with the project timeline.

sections.explain: English requires the 'dummy' subject 'It' for weather and time.

words.word: It is raining heavily outside.
Is raining heavily outside.
It raining heavily outside.

sections.explain: The verb 'explain' always requires 'to' before the person receiving the info.

words.word: Can you explain the rule to me?
Can you explain me the rule?
Can you explain the rule me?

sections.explain: 'Revert' means 'to return'. 'Revert back' is redundant logic.

words.word: Please revert by tomorrow morning.
Please revert back by tomorrow morning.
Please kindly revert back tomorrow.

sections.explain: You depend 'on' something. 'Depend of' is a literal translation error.

words.word: Success depends on hard work.
Success depends of hard work.
Success depends from hard work.

sections.explain: You 'discuss a topic'. Using 'discuss about' is a common South Asian error.

words.word: We need to discuss the new contract.
We need to discuss about the contract.
We need to discussion the contract.

sections.explain: In Global English, 'cousin' is gender-neutral. No need to add brother/sister.

words.word: He is my cousin from New York.
He is my cousin brother from New York.
He is a cousin brother of me.

sections.explain: In English, you 'are' an age. You don't 'have' years like in Spanish.

words.word: I am thirty years old.
I have thirty years old.
I have thirty years.

sections.explain: 'Suggest' is followed by a 'that' clause or -ing, never 'to + infinitive'.

words.word: I suggest that you arrive early.
I suggest you to arrive early.
I suggest to arrive early for you.
